name: 6e6a-woocommerce-35520

pr.title: Invalidate the coupon code lookup cache when a coupon is unpublished outside the CRUD
pr.body:
### Submission Review Guidelines:

-   I have followed the [WooCommerce Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/blob/trunk/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [WordPress Coding Standards](https://make.wordpress.org/core/handbook/best-practices/coding-standards/).
-   I have checked to ensure there aren't other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/pulls) for the same update/change.
-   I have reviewed my code for [security best practices](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/).
-   Following the above guidelines will result in quick merges and clear and detailed feedback when appropriate.

### Changes proposed in this Pull Request:

The coupon code lookup cache (`coupon_id_from_code`, used by `wc_get_coupon_id_by_code()`) was only invalidated through the WC_Coupon CRUD. Bulk edit, WP-CLI or direct `wp_update_post()` / `wp_delete_post()` calls left a stale entry behind, so draft, pending, private or trashed coupons stayed applicable on sites with a persistent object cache.

This PR adds `CouponCodeLookupInvalidator` (src/Internal/Caches), which owns the cache key and invalidates per coupon in two layers:

- On write, `transition_post_status` and `deleted_post` listeners delete the lookup entry of the coupon's stored code when it crosses the publish boundary or is deleted. Other coupons' entries stay warm.
- On read, `wc_get_coupon_id_by_code()` only serves a cached entry while every id in it is still a published coupon, checked through `get_post()`. WordPress cleans the post cache on every post write, so this also catches what deleting one key cannot reach: the same code cached under another key (raw vs sanitized, surrounding whitespace, or a spelling the accent-insensitive collation treats as equal, e.g. `café` for `cafe`) and a lookup that wrote a stale id back after the delete. Stale entries are removed.

The read check describes what `WC_Coupon_Data_Store_CPT` resolves, so it only runs while that data store is in use. A custom coupon data store keeps the write layer as its only coverage, what it had before this PR. The cache key is unchanged, so `WC_Cache_Helper::invalidate_cache_group( 'coupons' )` still reaches the entries.

Cost: one post cache read per cached id on a hit. The coupon data store reads the same post right after, so `new WC_Coupon( $code )` stays at the same query count (3 with a cold post cache). Callers that only resolve the id pay one extra query when the post cache is cold. Measured with 2,000 published coupons: +3 µs per lookup on a warm post cache.

Backward compatibility: additive. New internal class, new public methods and two hook listeners. No existing signatures, hooks or filters changed, and the lookup cache key format is unchanged.

Pre-existing limitation, not addressed here: renaming a published coupon's code keeps the old code resolving until the coupon is unpublished or the entry is evicted.

Closes #35520. Partial fix in PR #47739 covered only the CRUD path.

### How to test the changes in this Pull Request:

1. Create a published percentage coupon and a simple product.
2. As a guest, add the product to the cart, apply the coupon, then remove it.
3. In wp-admin > Marketing > Coupons, use Bulk actions > Edit to set the coupon to Draft.
4. On the cart, apply it again. It should be rejected with "cannot be applied because it does not exist."

Without a persistent object cache the stale entry does not survive between requests, so step 4 passes even on trunk. To reproduce in a single process:

```sh
wp eval '
$c = new WC_Coupon(); $c->set_code( "cli-test" ); $c->set_discount_type( "percent" ); $c->set_amount( 10 ); $c->save();
echo wc_get_coupon_id_by_code( "cli-test" ) . "\n"; // primes the cache
wp_update_post( array( "ID" => $c->get_id(), "post_status" => "draft" ) );
echo wc_get_coupon_id_by_code( "cli-test" ) . "\n"; // trunk: stale id, this PR: 0
'
```

### Testing that has already taken place:

- `CouponCodeLookupInvalidatorTest` covers unpublish, trash and delete outside the CRUD, other coupons staying warm, a stale late write being rejected, code aliases (raw entity, whitespace, accent, decomposed accent), the newest duplicate winning and the older one taking over again, a warm hit served without a query, a custom data store keeping its entries, and the `coupons` group invalidation still reaching the lookup entries. The data store's `save_post` invalidation is covered in `WC_Tests_Coupon_Data_Store`. Coupon, discounts, cart, totals and order suites pass (580 tests).
- Verified across real requests with a temporary file-backed persistent object cache: apply in the block cart, set to draft via WP-CLI, re-apply rejected. A stale entry written back after the draft is rejected and removed, and republishing makes the coupon apply again.
- Benchmarked against the prefix rotation version with 2,000 published coupons (numbers above), and query counts compared against `trunk` on a dev env with a persistent object cache.

commit_log:
Merge branch 'trunk' into fix/35520-stale-coupon-code-lookup-cache
�
Cover the coupon data store's save_post lookup invalidation
Core fires wp_transition_post_status() before save_post, so the listener has
already run by the time the CRUD writes the status with $wpdb. What the branch
actually covers is the case where the CRUD writes a different status than core
did, a save_post callback setting the coupon to draft for instance. Say that
instead of claiming it is the only write-side invalidation on the path, and add
the test that was missing so it cannot be dropped silently.

Also drop the strict_types declaration this branch added to the file. It is
unrelated to the fix and applies to every other test in it.

Addresses review feedback on PR #66900.
�
Skip the coupon lookup read check for custom data stores
is_lookup_entry_stale() describes what WC_Coupon_Data_Store_CPT resolves, so a
store registered through woocommerce_data_stores that resolves other statuses,
or coupons that are not posts at all, had every entry it wrote rejected by the
next read. Measured with a store that also resolves private coupons: one query
per lookup, where before this branch the entry was served from cache. Gate the
check on the core data store so those sites keep the write-side hooks as their
only layer, the coverage they had before.

Also drop the dedicated 'coupon_code_lookups' prefix namespace. Its only
production caller was the 4.5.0 code sanitization migration, which now rotates
the 'coupons' group prefix through invalidate_all(). That takes a wp_cache_get
and ~48 bytes off every lookup key, and makes the key byte-identical to the one
before this branch again, so extension code that rebuilt it by hand still
matches.

Addresses review feedback on PR #66900.
�
Replace the lookup namespace rotation with a per-coupon read-time check
�
Document what rotating the lookup namespace costs
Rotation drops the whole store's lookup cache, and the CRUD's trash and delete
paths go through the same hooks, so a store that churns coupons keeps the cache
mostly empty and pays for get_ids_by_code() on every miss. Spell that out next
to why the cheaper single-key delete is not enough.

Addresses review feedback on PR #66900.
�
Drop the redundant lookup invalidation from the force-delete branch
Core only reroutes 'post' and 'page' to the trash when the force flag is off,
so wp_delete_post() really deletes a shop_coupon and fires deleted_post, which
CouponCodeLookupInvalidator already listens to. The manual call was also the
weaker of the two, since it only reached the sanitized form of the code.

Addresses review feedback on PR #66900.
�
Explain why the coupon data store still invalidates the lookup cache itself
The manual invalidate() call reads as redundant now that transition_post_status
is listened to, but the doing_action( 'save_post' ) branch writes the status
with $wpdb directly, so no transition fires and this is the only invalidation
on that path.
�
Nest the coupons group prefix inside the coupon lookup cache key
Moving the lookup keys under their own prefix namespace made
WC_Cache_Helper::invalidate_cache_group( 'coupons' ) a silent no-op for them,
which was the only invalidation idiom extensions had. Nesting the group prefix
outside the lookup prefix keeps that working, the way
WC_Data::generate_meta_cache_key() has nested since 4.7.0. The cache group also
gets an accessor so wc_get_coupon_id_by_code() no longer hardcodes it next to a
key it gets from the invalidator.
�
Narrow the coupon lookup invalidation to the transitions that can change it
wp_insert_post() reports 'new' as the old status, so every published coupon
creation was rotating the whole store's lookup namespace, and deleted_post had
no status guard at all. Rotate only when a coupon leaves publish or a published
coupon is deleted; entering publish invalidates just that code, which still
covers a newer duplicate taking over an already cached code.
�
Declare strict_types in the coupon data store test file
�
Guard the transition_post_status handler against non-WP_Post values
�
Invalidate the coupon code lookup cache in the 4.5.0 code-sanitization migration
�
Rotate a dedicated lookup namespace instead of deleting a single key
Give the coupon code to id lookup its own 'coupon_code_lookups' prefix
namespace and rotate it on the publish boundary or deletion, rather than
deleting one exact key. This also invalidates entries primed under a
different code representation (raw vs sanitized) and strands a lookup
still in progress from writing a stale id back, while leaving the meta
cache shared by every WC_Coupon in the 'coupons' group untouched.

Addresses review feedback on PR #66900.
�
Invalidate the coupon code lookup cache when a coupon is unpublished outside the CRUD
The coupon code to id lookup cache was only invalidated when a coupon was
unpublished or deleted through the WC_Coupon CRUD. Status changes made via
bulk edit, WP-CLI or direct wp_update_post()/wp_delete_post() calls left a
stale entry behind, keeping draft, pending, private or trashed coupons
applicable on sites with a persistent object cache.

Introduce CouponCodeLookupInvalidator, which owns the cache key building
and listens to transition_post_status and deleted_post to cover the paths
that bypass the CRUD. The coupon data store and wc_get_coupon_id_by_code()
now delegate to it.
�
